title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity (params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability)
author: Alex Kim
description: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer and streaming path to parity for /v1/chat.completions. This change implements parameter mapping (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), explicit role handling for assistant/system/user, legacy 'stop' token behavior, and optional logprobs passthrough. It also stabilizes streaming by buffering token fragments and normalizing chunk boundaries to match expected OpenAI event sequences. Includes adjustments to response formatting to maintain deterministic JSON structure when structured_output or function calls are used. Motivation: customers depend on OpenAI-compatible clients and test suites; mismatches in param semantics, role ordering, stop token handling, and streaming chunk boundaries caused user-facing regressions and compatibility test failures. This PR: 1) Adds full params translation layer with validation and backwards-compatible defaults. 2) Preserves role order and supplies missing role normalization for older model variants. 3) Implements stop sequence semantics (inclusive/exclusive variants) and integrates with KV-cache to avoid accidental token leakage. 4) Exposes logprobs when requested through the compat layer and adds safe size limits. 5) Harmonizes streaming framing so clients receive the same sequence of data and final delta messages as OpenAI. 6) Adds tests (unit + integration) and docs updates. Checklist: - [x] Param mapping and validation - [x] Role normalization and tests - [x] Stop sequence implementation and KV-cache safety - [x] Logprobs passthrough with size guard - [x] Streaming stability fixes and tests - [x] SDK compatibility (python/ts) - [x] Docs and release notes
